pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-01.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 3 panels: a wide top tier, a tall bottom-left panel and a tall bottom-right panel. There are grey placeholder boxes labelled ananya and meera. No order numbers or guide lines appear.
pages.observation: My natural reading order was P1 -> P2 -> P3. P1 has the caption 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' and a small ananya placeholder. P2 has two balloons, both read as Meera's: 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...' then 'I wish everything were easier to manage!'. The left balloon is read first. Its tail is long and ends in empty space just left of and above Meera's box rather than on her, but she is the only person in the panel. P3 has Ananya saying 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.', with a clear tail to her, and Meera sits small at lower left. The exchange reads naturally as a complaint followed by the doctor's answer. Issues: (1) Meera's role is never shown or stated (receptionist? staff?), so a first reader does not know who she is relative to Ananya. (2) P1 is a large establishing panel with only a caption and one tiny figure. In P2 and P3 all text and figures sit in the top half, leaving the bottom halves of both tall panels empty, which makes the page feel unbalanced. The layout needs a staging or size rethink rather than just filling the space. (3) The first balloon's tail does not end on Meera.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 4 panels: a wide top panel, a middle row split into a wider left and narrower right panel, and a wide bottom panel. There are two teal label boxes.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1 caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' (top-left), then the teal label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic' (top-right). Next came P2, Ananya: 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' Then P3, Meera: 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.', followed by the label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff' at the bottom of P3. Last was P4: 'One team. Better coordination.', whose short tail points left to Ananya, with Meera on the right. All speakers were clear and the 'And our team...' line follows naturally from Ananya's line. Issues: (1) It is never shown what Welbuk is (software, a service?). 'Onboarding' and 'here' have nothing visible in the storyboard to refer to, so the reader needs a screen or device in P1/P2 to make 'here' concrete. (2) The P1 caption box and teal label sit flush against or overlap the top panel border. (3) In P4 the balloon covers Ananya's placeholder label ('anany...') and sits very close to her face area. Her face placement needs checking. (4) The time jump from the page 1 conversation to the onboarding has no time cue beyond the caption.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 5 panels: two rows of two, then a wide bottom panel. There are placeholders for raman, meera, priya and ravi. Panel 4 has no figure, and there is one teal screen label.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1 'The front desk is always an option.' (raman and meera), P2 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' (priya), P3 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' (ravi), P4 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' (no figure, presumably a phone insert), and P5 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' with the screen label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12' above raman, priya and ravi from left to right. The page is all captions. I read the three slots as matching the three check-in methods in order, so A-12 is Ravi, which is consistent with page 4. Issues: (1) P1 opens with 'always an option' before the reader knows the topic is patient check-in. The word 'check in' first appears in P2, so the first caption reads out of context. (2) Raman and Priya are never named on the page, so the reader only learns the names from Ravi's caption. (3) The app check-in 'ahead' (P2) and the QR scan at the door (P3) both happen on a phone, so the difference needs to be visible in the art (at home vs. at the door). (4) There is no transition from the staff onboarding on page 2 to patients arriving, such as a time or location cue. (5) P4 has no figure, so the phone or hand insert needs to be specified.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 3 panels: a wide top panel, then tall bottom-left and bottom-right panels. There are placeholders for ravi, nurse and ananya, and two teal screen labels.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1 caption 'Soon, his slot comes up.' then the screen label 'NOW · A-12' (ravi). 'his' resolves to Ravi from the end of page 3 and A-12 matches. P2 has the caption 'A quick vitals check first.' then the nurse's balloon 'Let's check your vitals, Ravi.', whose long tail goes down to the nurse, with Ravi at lower left. P3 has the caption 'Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready.' and the label 'RAVI · READY' below Ananya. The order and speakers were clear. Issues: (1) The P2 caption and the nurse's line say the same thing, so one could be cut. (2) The nurse is unnamed and was not shown on the earlier pages. That is acceptable, but nothing identifies her as a nurse beyond the placeholder, so the art must show it. (3) Both tall bottom panels again have large empty lower areas. (4) In P3, whether Ananya is looking at a device to receive the notification needs to be shown, because it is not obvious that the 'RAVI · READY' label is on a screen she is viewing.

It shows 4 panels: a wide top panel, a middle row of two, and a wide bottom panel. There are placeholders for ananya and ravi. In P2 and P3 one person's position is shown only as a dot marker with no box.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1, Ananya (left): 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.', with Ravi on the right. Next came P2, Ravi: 'I've been feeling tired lately.', whose tail points to his box. Then P3 caption: 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' (Ananya's box). Last was P4, Ananya: 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.', with Ravi on the right. Ananya stays left and Ravi right across the panels, so the left-right staging is consistent and the exchange reads naturally. Issues: (1) In P2, Ananya appears only as a marker at the far left with no face box. In P3, Ravi appears only as a marker at the right panel edge with no box. It is unclear whether these faces are visible, offscreen or cut off, and this needs to be decided and recorded. (2) In P1 and P4 the balloons cover Ananya's placeholder label and sit right against her box, which could cover her face. (3) The P3 narrator caption interrupts the doctor-patient exchange with a slogan. It reads as an advertising aside, not a story beat. (4) Ravi's symptom ('tired') gets no specific follow-up, and Ananya's reply is generic. This is acceptable if it matches the source, but the exchange feels thin.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-06.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 4 panels: a wide top panel, a middle row of two, and a wide bottom panel. There are placeholders for meera, ravi and ananya, and one teal label.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1, Meera: 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' (Ravi on the right). Next came P2, Ravi: 'So I can keep useful information in one place?', followed by the label 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients'. Then P3, Meera: 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' Last was the P4 caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' with ananya, meera and ravi. The question and answer read in the right order and the speakers were clear. Issues: (1) It is confusing that page 5 ends in the consultation with Ananya and page 6 opens with Meera talking to Ravi, with no location or time cue (after the visit? at the front desk?). (2) Meera says 'Let's walk through what is available' but nothing on the page shows that walkthrough, so the promise is left hanging before the closing caption. (3) In P3, Ravi appears only as a marker at the right edge and his label crosses the panel border, so his face visibility and position are unresolved. (4) In P4, Meera's box overlaps Ananya's placeholder label ('anany'), so the figures are crowded and the purpose of the three-person group shot is unclear. (5) Ravi used the QR code rather than the app on page 3, so being introduced to Welbuk Health here is consistent. But the app was already named on page 3, so it is not explained why he is learning about it only now.

pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-07.png with Read and looked at it before reading any other document. The image loaded and was readable. It shows 4 panels: a top row of two, a wide middle panel and a tall wide bottom panel. There are placeholders for ravi, specialist, partner, child, meera and ananya, and several teal labels.
pages.observation: My reading order was P1 caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' (ravi). Next came P2, with the label 'WELBUK VISION' (top-left), the specialist, then the caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' Then P3, with the label 'WELBUK VISION' again, then 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' beside ravi, partner and child. Last was P4, with the label 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' (top-right) above meera, ananya and ravi, then the bottom caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' There are no spoken lines. Issues: (1) It is unclear whose voice 'us' and 'our hometown' are in P1: Ravi's thought, a narrator or the brand. (2) The specialist, partner and child appear for the first time with nothing to introduce them or show their relationship to Ravi, and nothing in the storyboard signals a different location for the specialist. (3) The 'WELBUK VISION' label appears twice in a row (P2 and P3), which is redundant. The P2 label also sits flush against or overlaps the panel border. (4) In P4 the label box overlaps Ravi's placeholder and label ('rav'), which could cover his face. (5) P4 leaves a large empty middle area between the figures and the bottom caption. (6) The page switches from story to pure brand messaging. It reads as an advertisement ending rather than a narrative close, so the transition from page 6 needs more than the word 'Tomorrow'.
